title: Yichuan Liu, MIT 15.401 Finance Theory I — Recitation 2: Fixed-Income Securities (slides dated 2010, hosted with Fall 2008 course)
use: Scoped companion for spot/forward relations, coupon-bond yield versus date-specific discounting, dated cash-flow replication, and Macaulay/modified-duration and dollar-exposure terminology. All chapter cases, proofs, numerical values and exercises are original.
verification: Actual official 29-page PDF body inspected, especially PDF pages 2–4, 15–18 and 20; author/date labels read as Yichuan Liu/2010. Extraction around formulas is imperfect; chapter formulas are independently derived. The apparent negative convexity sign at PDF page 19 and any claim of perfect general immunization are not adopted. No source example or historical market observation is reused.

title: TreasuryDirect — Buying a Treasury Marketable Security, scoped accrued-interest explanation
use: Official illustration that accrued interest can enter the purchase payment and be included in a later coupon. The chapter specifies its own fictional settlement/day-count/entitlement contracts rather than prescribing current Treasury trading rules.
verification: Actual official HTML inspected at the accrued-interest introduction and More about paying accrued interest in the purchase price, retrieved lines 43–45 and 124–136. Account eligibility, limits, timing, tax, settlement and auction rules are outside the cited scope.

title: Nicola Anderson and John Sleath — New estimates of the UK real and nominal yield curves, Bank of England Working Paper 126 (2001)
use: Finite quoted bonds require a curve-fitting assumption between cash-flow dates; fit, smoothness and stability answer different evaluation questions. Used for a bounded research-design critique, not as evidence that one estimator is universally best.
verification: Actual official 41-page PDF inspected at printed pages 7–11 (PDF pages 3–7), including the discount-function cash-flow relation, finite-maturity identification issue, and stated smoothness/flexibility/stability criteria. Empirical UK estimates, historical institutional facts and the later spline implementation/results are not imported. Original chapter interpolation and perturbation cases are independently derived.
